description: Read and act on X (Twitter) through the full X API v2: publish and search posts, read timelines, mentions, likes, bookmarks and followers, look up and search users, send and read Direct Messages and encrypted Chat, manage Lists, Spaces, Communities, trends, news, Community Notes, live broadcasts and media uploads, and run usage, compliance and webhook routes (259 operations).

api.description: Creates an X Developer Platform account for the authenticated user if they do not already have one, and returns it. Idempotent: when the user already has an account it is returned unchanged with `created` false. Needs a user (OAuth 2.0) token. Needs the extra OAuth scope developer.write (pass scopes to the plugin).

fields.description: Optional provisioning-credit metadata (an opaque string, e.g. a subscription tier) to claim for the account, attributed to the calling app. Omit to just ensure the account.

api.description: Creates a bot account in the calling app's project and returns its bearer token. Repeating the request for a handle the project already has returns that bot with a new token and revokes the previous one, so a retry can revoke a token another caller just received. Coordinate retries for the same handle.

fields.description: The bot's display name; defaults to the handle.
The bot's handle (X screen name): 5-15 characters, letters, numbers, or underscores.

Whether only members of the bot's developer account can add it to group chats. An org-only bot has no public profile and doesn't appear in public search. Everyone in its developer account should be able to message it, so leave its Direct Messages open to everyone rather than premium senders only. Defaults to false. Applies only when the request creates the bot: a handle that already names one of the project's bots keeps that bot's setting, which the response's org_only reports.

Scopes for the bot's bearer token. Broadcast moderation additionally supports broadcast.read and broadcast.write. Defaults to the XChat scope set (dm.read, dm.write, tweet.read, users.read, media.write).

Invitees get an email unless notify_invitees is false. Invitees get an email unless notify_invitees is false. Needs a user (OAuth 2.0) token. Whether the user's subscribers can always message them regardless of allow_dms_from.

api.description: Appends one segment of the file to a chunked upload. Send the segment base64-encoded in media (raw bytes in multipart bodies) and its position in the file in segment_index, counting from 0. A segment can be up to 8 MB; in a JSON body keep it to 4 MB or less, because base64 adds a third. After the last segment, call Finalize Media Upload. Pass media as { base64: "…" }, { url } or a public URL string (a bare string is a URL, not base64); the plugin base64-encodes the bytes for X. Up to 4 MB per segment. Needs a user (OAuth 2.0) token.

api.description: Uploads a media file in one request and returns its id. Send the file base64-encoded in media (raw bytes in multipart bodies). For a Post, set media_category to tweet_image (JPG, PNG, GIF or WEBP, up to 5 MB) or tweet_gif, then pass the returned id in media.media_ids on Create or Edit Post. DM media uses dm_image or dm_gif. For video, use Initialize Media Upload. Pass media as { base64: "…" }, { url } or a public URL string (a bare string is a URL, not base64); the plugin base64-encodes the bytes for X. Up to 15 MB here; use the chunked upload (initialize, append, finalize) for video. Needs a user (OAuth 2.0) token.

Skip the announcing Post. Unset keeps the broadcast's setting, which defaults to posting. `"true"`, `"false"`, `1` and `0` are also accepted. `PUBLISH` only.
`PUBLISH` or `END`.
Broadcast title. `PUBLISH` only.
